key_themes: AI/semiconductor rotation: chip stocks sink after 80%+ H1 rally as investors question sustainability
Healthcare sector surge: CMS proposes 2.4% Medicare home health payment increase for 2027
Jobs miss + Fed signal: June payrolls 57k vs 113k expected; Warsh says inflation risks eased substantially

stocks.discussion_driver: Rivian delivered 12,194 vehicles in Q2 2026, beating estimates, and raised full-year 2026 guidance to 65,000-70,000 units. The stock surged 12.9% on July 2 to $19.39, pushing above the analyst consensus price target of $18.19. The delivery beat signals Rivian's production ramp is gaining momentum, though the company remains unprofitable and analysts may now lag the stock until they revise targets higher.
bull_case: Q2 delivery beat and raised full-year guidance signal accelerating production ramp and improving operational execution
New R2 SUV platform launch opens the mass-market EV segment and could dramatically expand Rivian's addressable market
bear_case: Company remains deeply unprofitable with significant ongoing cash burn; stock now trading above analyst consensus price target after the surge
Intense competition from Tesla, legacy automakers, and subsidized Chinese EV manufacturers threatens long-term market position

stocks.discussion_driver: Sandisk plunged 10-12% on July 2 amid a broad semiconductor selloff as fears of AI-trade overextension intensified, led by declines in Korean chip stocks. The stock has fallen ~25% from its June 25 all-time high despite bullish analyst targets of $2,500-$3,250, creating tension between near-term memory supply-glut fears and long-term AI storage demand tailwinds.
bull_case: AI data centers require exponentially more NAND flash storage, driving long-term secular demand growth for Sandisk's core products
Major bank price targets of $2,500-$3,250 (Susquehanna $3,250, Bernstein $3,000, BofA $2,500) suggest ~50%+ upside from current levels
bear_case: Elevated trailing P/E ratio of 70-75x leaves minimal margin for error in earnings execution amid macro uncertainty
Memory chip supply glut fears and Korean chip sector contagion could prolong near-term selling pressure

stocks.discussion_driver: Teradyne fell 9-13% on July 2 in the broad semiconductor sector selloff, reversing some of its remarkable 111%+ year-to-date gain driven by record Q1 2026 results and AI-driven semiconductor testing demand. Recent analyst upgrades from Cantor Fitzgerald and Susquehanna to $550 price targets signal long-term conviction, while the stock's elevated 56-64x forward P/E leaves it exposed to valuation compression in a risk-off environment.
bull_case: AI-driven semiconductor testing demand driving record revenues; Nasdaq-100 inclusion brings structural institutional buying demand
Robotics division (Universal Robots) provides non-semiconductor revenue diversification and reduces cyclicality risk
bear_case: Trades at 56-64x forward P/E following a 111%+ YTD run, creating significant vulnerability to multiple compression during sector rotations
Analyst consensus price target of $393.92 sits just 5.3% above current price, limiting near-term upside if semiconductor sentiment stays negative

stocks.discussion_driver: Corning fell 10-13% on July 2 after hitting an all-time high of $271.78 on June 30, dragged lower by the AI infrastructure selloff alongside chip equipment peers. The stock has surged 391% over the past year on surging demand for its fiber optic and photonic products for AI data centers. However, the stock trades 14.6% above analyst consensus price targets and at a trailing P/E exceeding 90x, raising material valuation concerns.
bull_case: AI data center buildout driving unprecedented demand for optical fiber; new Photonics MAP platform targeting Gen AI OEMs expected to generate significant revenue growth through 2030
Recent FTSE Russell index reconstitution added Corning to growth benchmarks, potentially attracting new long-term institutional capital
bear_case: Stock trading 14.6% above analyst consensus price target of $192.64 even after the July 2 selloff, with trailing P/E above 90x — extreme valuation risk
Production bottlenecks and costly maintenance shutdown at its newly separated solar wafer facility create near-term earnings risk

stocks.discussion_driver: Applied Materials plunged approximately 10% on July 2 in a sector-wide semiconductor equipment selloff as investors questioned the sustainability of AI infrastructure buildout valuations. The selloff follows AMAT hitting an all-time intraday high of $739.67 on June 30. Despite the decline, major banks recently raised price targets to $715-$900, and the company holds a Strong Buy consensus from 39 analysts, suggesting the pullback may represent a buying opportunity.
bull_case: Dominant semiconductor equipment market position with deep exposure to the AI chip manufacturing capex cycle driving long-term revenue growth
Recent analyst upgrades from BofA ($720), Wells Fargo ($715), and Susquehanna ($900) signal strong institutional conviction in the multi-year AI buildout thesis
bear_case: Semiconductor equipment spending is highly cyclical; any deceleration in AI capex by hyperscalers could cause sharp revenue and multiple contraction
Stock is down ~16% from its all-time high with negative sector sentiment; formal analyst consensus target was last measured below current price
